newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins steady, eye closely Brady,US bonds.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins steady, eye closely Brady,US bonds.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds, which recently set historic records, were steady compared with late Tuesday but dealers said on Wednesday prices were fluctuating on nervousness about moves in Brady and U.S. bonds.
News U.S. consumer prices rose only modestly in June provided more ground for speculative swaying, they said.
MinFins set records in early July when the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) left interest rates unchanged, and prices set new consecutive records for a week, until profit-taking set in.
"Prices firmed right after figures but selling, apparently speculative, started right away. MinFins are edging up once again at the moment," National Reserve Bank dealer Andrei Ivanov-Golitsyn said.
The U.S. Labor Department reported on Wednesday the CPI rose 0.1 percent in June, compared with a forecast gain of 0.2 percent and a 0.1 percent rise in May.

Dealers said the market was otherwise overshadowed by the downward trend in other emerging debt. Brady bond dealers said earlier fears that Brazil might be forced to devalue shook local stock markets, and debt prices fell too.

"London was seen selling (MinFins) in early trade, while bids on screens were mainly from Russian banks," Sberbank dealer Sergei Abramov said. "West could prefer to stay short either ahead of figures or looking at other debt."
Dealers were reluctant to forecast moves of MinFins, being almost 100 percent dependent on trends in U.S. and Brady bonds
